statement: Suppose µ− ⪯ µ+ are two ordered laws, possibly on different volumes or with different pins. Assume there is a common unpinned source contour S0 such that, given its spins, both laws have the same critical nearest-neighbor continuation toward T. Apart from the common pinning data, this continuation has zero field. All changed data lie on the source side of S0. For an admissible intermediate cut J, there are C < ∞ and θ ∈ (0, 1/8) such that ‖ ‖ ‖µ+ T − µ− T ‖ ‖ ‖ TV ≤ C(w/s)−7/8+θ( Eµ+ MJ − Eµ− MJ ) . (2.4) Here total variation is the supremum of event-probability differences. The constants depend on the fixed chart and admissibility constants, not on the source values or their number. At a fixed positive w/s, vanishing rescaled magnetic difference implies vanishing target total variation. Random ordered source configurations are allowed.
